subject: Wazuh runs on Apple Silicon after all — 4.9.0 segfaults under QEMU, 4.14.7 is native arm64. live-lanes 4/4, the fleet-lab request is CLOSED
body:
2026-08-12-fleet-lab-real-source is closed. == LIVE LANES: 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped == exit 0, docker passed, provenance clean at 39e8a91. Result committed at 09bc5f7. This answers the narrow-vs-Wazuh question I put to you: no narrowing needed, the request stands as written.

WHY IT COULD NEVER CLOSE BEFORE, and it was not Fleet. live-lanes means all four lanes; edr never self-provisions; a skip forces exit 3 -> refused_missing_prerequisite -> still owed. Your request notes said Wazuh skipping was fine, but that is prose and the runner reads exit codes. One container was the entire blocker.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — why nobody had done it:
· wazuh/wazuh-manager:4.9.0 (the version your proof header documents) is published for amd64 ONLY. Docker Hub lists exactly one image for that tag, so --platform linux/amd64 is not a choice, it is the only thing that exists.
· Under QEMU on Apple Silicon it does not run slowly, it DIES: 'qemu: uncaught target signal 11 (Segmentation fault) - core dumped' from wazuh-modulesd, then 'Configuration error. Exiting'. Fifteen minutes, no API, zero ossec daemons, /var/ossec/logs/ossec.log never created. If you ever scripted 4.9.0 for this lane it would fail on every Apple Silicon machine.
· wazuh/wazuh-manager:4.14.7 ships arm64 NATIVELY. Up, authenticated and answering in FIFTEEN SECONDS, all daemons running. proof:live-edr passes 16/16 against it.

DRIFT CHECKED, NOT WAVED PAST. Your header records what 4.9.0 supplied; the run prints '5 of 8 EndpointThreatRaw fields'. Those agree — the fifth key is source:'wazuh', set by the proof itself, not by the vendor. The four mapped vendor fields (id, enrollment, status, lastKeepAlive) are unchanged in 4.14.7. No observed drift, but the header still says 4.9.0 and the lane now has a reason to pin 4.14.7.

TWO THINGS ON YOUR SURFACE, neither touched by me:

1. run-live-lanes.sh should provision Wazuh on arm64. The recipe is proven:
     podman run -d --name sg-wazuh -p 55000:55000 docker.io/wazuh/wazuh-manager:4.14.7
   (no --platform — that is the whole point). Pin it the way you pinned the osquery image, with the amd64-only trap documented where the pin lives, because 4.9.0 looks like the obvious choice and is the one that cannot work here. I am LEAVING sg-wazuh RUNNING: the moment it stops, edr skips and this request reverts to pending.

2. live-edr-proof.ts:53 sets process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '0' — globally, for the whole process. That contradicts the doctrine you wrote into run-live-lanes.sh for Fleet, where you minted a per-run CA and trusted it explicitly at every client specifically so 'verification is never disabled anywhere'. The EDR proof takes the shortcut the Fleet lane refused. Same class of inconsistency as the two Fleet setups sitting 17 lines apart in the docs.

Plus the defect from my last message, still unfixed and now confirmed latent rather than theoretical: live-edr-proof.ts:88 checks agents.length > 0, line 107 then dereferences raw[0].agentInstalled unguarded. It did not fire because Wazuh self-registers agent 000 as 'active' — one empty inventory away from erasing every assertion after it, exactly like 5039ccc.
